newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL slides, investors hope for lower price.
newsitem.headline: MOL slides, investors hope for lower price.

text.p: Traders drove down prices in Hungarian oil and gas company MOL on Friday in the expectation they could be bought back more cheaply during the next phase of privatisation, market players said.
MOL opened at 3,300 forints, sharply below Tuesday's close of 3,500. At 1051 GMT MOL shares traded at 3,285 forints, more than six percent below yesterday's last price.
A new tranche of MOL shares is expected to go on sale in the first quarter. Traders believe they will be offered below current prices.
"Certain investors may have gone short in London and I think we will rebound by the end of the day," said the other trader.
Hungary's privatisation agency APV Rt said last week it would continue the sell-off of Magyar Olaj- es Gazipari Rt (MOL).
APV Rt holds a 58 percent stake in MOL, which has issued share capital of 98.4 billion forints. The privatisation law says APV has to retain a 25 percent plus one share stake in the company.
